newsitem.title: USA: NABE sees continued strength in U.S economy.
newsitem.headline: NABE sees continued strength in U.S economy.

text.p: U.S. industry demand has firmed in the second quarter of the year, suggesting continued healthy economic growth, a 131-member panel of the National Association of Business Economists (NABE) said on Wednesday.

"Demand accelerated in the second quarter after slowing some in the first, pointing to continued underlying strength in the economy," the business group said in its latest report on U.S. business conditions.
NABE said 58.8 percent of respondents in its quarterly survey had reported rising unit demand, up from 48.4 percent in the last report. Just 4.6 percent reported falling demand.
While demand remained strong, NABE said only a few of its panelists had reported higher prices -- two-thirds of respondents reported prices were unchanged in the April-June period.
"These responses continue to reflect a very competitive business environment where price increases are increasingly difficult to realize," the group said.
Still, profit margins continued to improve in the second quarter on the back of lower material costs and restrained labor costs, the survey showed.

Corresponding to a continued rise in demand, NABE firms also reported rising employment levels. More than 34 percent of respondents said they had added jobs in the period, while just 10.7 percent reported falling employment levels.
"This very strong second quarter 1997 employment performance points to continued healthy income gains, strong consumer confidence and renewed consumer spending," the survey said.
NABE said 41.5 percent of firms expected a "somewhat higher" level of employment over the next six months, while 43.8 percent of firms said their employment level should be "about the same."

However, firms also reported that the labor market was getting increasingly tight and that trained labor was difficult to find. Some 58 percent of the panelists reported difficulties in hiring skilled labor, primarily in the area of information processing.

The group said a majority of firms surveyed -- 72.5 percent -- expected "average" economic growth for 1998, while 22.1 percent expected "sluggish" growth. "Strong" growth was expected by 5.3 percent of those who responded, while none of the panelists feared a recession, NABE added.
